concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish growth as a quantitative, value-neutral change from development as a qualitative, value-positive change.
Explain why measuring development only by economic growth ignores changes in people's lives.
Describe the contributions of Mahbub-ul-Haq and Amartya Sen to the idea of human development.
Identify health, education and access to resources as the key areas of human development.
Explain how a lack of capability in health, education or resources limits people's choices.

topics.title: The four pillars of human development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain equity as equal access to opportunities irrespective of gender, race, income and caste.
Explain sustainability as continuity in the availability of opportunities across generations.
Explain productivity as human work efficiency and empowerment as the power to make choices.
Compare the income approach and the welfare approach to human development.
Compare the basic needs approach of the ILO with the capability approach of Amartya Sen.
Identify the indicators and weightage used in the human development index and interpret its scores.
Explain the human poverty index as a non-income measure of the shortfall in human development.
Describe Bhutan's Gross National Happiness as an alternative measure of progress.
Classify countries into very high, high, medium and low human development using HDI scores.
Explain why territorial size and per capita income are not directly related to human development.
Analyse how social-sector spending, political stability, freedom and equity shape human development levels.
